history.t: First release. Five gauges, from 2023 through early October 2026.

money.reading: The four biggest spenders put $171B into capex last quarter, 79% more than a year earlier. Growth is still speeding up: a year before, it was 64%. Their 2026 guidance adds up to roughly $720–745B, against $414B in 2025. Oracle is spending like a fifth hyperscaler, with $28.5B in its June–August quarter alone.
money.watch: A big-four company cuts its 2026 range, or 2027 plans come in flat.

chips.reading: Nvidia’s data center business brought in $89B last quarter, more than double a year ago, and the growth rate rose from 56% to 117%. Management calls next year’s roughly 70% growth “supply-constrained,” and the CFO named memory as the scarce input, so the bottleneck sits below the GPU. Press estimates have TSMC’s CoWoS packaging capacity more than doubling from 2025 to 2027.
chips.watch: Data center growth drops below 50% a year while packaging capacity keeps climbing. Then demand, not supply, is the limit.
thesis: The bottleneck moved below the GPU.

quotes.who: Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO, at GTC
quotes.q: I see through 2027, at least $1 trillion.
quotes.note: TechCrunch reported this as expected Blackwell and Vera Rubin orders through 2027.

quotes.who: Colette Kress, Nvidia CFO, on the earnings call
quotes.q: We expect to grow revenue by approximately 70% in fiscal 2028. This is a supply-constrained outlook.
quotes.note: Fiscal 2028 runs from February 2027 to January 2028.

buildings.reading: A record 7.5 GW was under construction in CBRE’s primary markets in the first half of 2026, up 43% in a year. Vacancy held at 1.4%, the lowest reading in this series. The biggest single campuses are now measured in gigawatts, and most of them are still being built.
buildings.watch: Vacancy back above 3%, or construction falling for two halves in a row.

power.reading: GE Vernova’s gas turbine queue more than doubled in a year, to 116 GW of orders and slot reservations, and it is now selling slots for 2032. Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi are booked years out too. So buyers are also going around the queue: restarting reactors, paying for uprates and buying fuel cells. Most of the new gas plants they back are in the queue themselves.
power.watch: Reservations stop converting to firm orders, or open 2029–30 slots start to pile up.
thesis: The power plant that ships like a server.

compute.reading: If the world were overbuilding, rents would be falling. They’re rising. Silicon Data’s H100 index is up about 40% since December and its B200 index is up about a third this year. In April, SemiAnalysis reported on-demand capacity sold out across all GPU types, based on checks with providers.
compute.watch: H100 rent back below $2 an hour, the Dec 9 reading, while B200 rents keep rising. That would mean old chips are being dumped, not moving down the menu.
thesis: Old GPUs don’t die. They move down the menu.

visibility.text: Colette Kress (CFO), Q2 FY2027 earnings call: "We expect to grow revenue by approximately 70% in fiscal 2028." "This is a supply-constrained outlook." Supply expected "to remain a bottleneck, at least through the end of fiscal year '28." On Vera Rubin: production shipments began in August, "having already received purchase orders from every major hyperscaler, AI cloud and system OEM". Jensen Huang: "Even though our demand is much greater than 70%, our supply allows us to confidently deliver 70%."

visibility.note: Kress quotes taken from third-party call transcripts (roic.ai; The Motley Fool transcript hosted on Webull), not an official NVIDIA transcript; 70% figure corroborated by Fortune and Axios (Aug 26, 2026). FY2028 = Feb 2027 to Jan 2028. A growth guide, not a bookings figure. Not in the Q2 FY27 CFO Commentary or press release.

capacity.text: Jul 22, 2026: GE Vernova said it has 'completed actions to deliver 20 GW of annual gas turbine production and on track for 24 GW in '28', and is 'utilizing lean and incremental machinery in existing factory footprint to reach 30 GW in '30'. The CEO said this is 'all funded by customer down payments.' The earlier unit-based target was '70 to 80 heavy-duty gas turbines per year beginning in the second half of 2026, up from 48 this year [2024]' (Jan 22, 2025). The Dec 9, 2025 update tied ~24 GW in 2028 to '90 - 100 heavy-duty gas units'.

history.text: CEO: 'we have now secured capacity to deliver between 70 to 80 heavy-duty gas turbines per year starting in 2026'; 'we are adding more capacity for Gas, from the 55 to the 70 to 80 a year'; 'probably on the lower end in '26, the higher end beyond that.'

CEO: 'expansion plans to produce 70 to 80 heavy-duty gas turbines per year beginning in the second half of 2026, up from 48 this year' and 'ramp to ship approximately 20 gigawatts annually starting in 2027, and expect to remain at that level going forward.'
CEO: 'reaching 20 GW of annualized deliveries in the second half of 2026 ... sustaining 20 GW per year, starting in 2027.'
Investor update: 'On track to increase annual gas turbine capacity to 20 GW in mid '26'; 'Implementing actions to raise production to ~24 GW in '28, including 90 - 100 heavy-duty gas units.'

Release: 'we remain on track to deliver 20 GW of annual gas turbine output in the third quarter of 2026, with 24 GW in 2028, and we are implementing actions to produce 30 GW in 2030.' On the call the CEO said GE Vernova had 'now reached our 20-gigawatt annualized run rate.'

Laguna conference, CEO: 'We will hit the five-gigawatt run rate for the third quarter and the fourth quarter of this year.' He said output steps up to 6 GW per quarter in 2H 2027, possibly stays at 6 GW for a period in 2028, then reaches 7 GW per quarter; 'we've installed over 350 new machines into our gas factories.'

peers.text: On its fiscal Q3 2026 pre-close call, Siemens Energy said its gas turbine order backlog was 'about 60 GW' at the end of fiscal Q2 (Mar 31, 2026). It expects '90 GW to 100 GW of total commitments' (orders plus reservation agreements) by the end of fiscal 2026 (Sep 30, 2026). It is 'booked out' until fiscal 2028, and 2029 and 2030 slots are 'filling up very quickly'. Fiscal Q2 gas turbine orders were a record EUR 8.9bn. It raised its market outlook to 110-120 GW of gas turbine additions a year.

Q3 FY2026 earnings release (quarter to Jun 30, 2026): 'Growth was driven by a new record order intake at Gas Services.' The full release reports Gas Services orders of EUR 9,967m (+61.9% comparable), a book-to-bill ratio of 2.65 and a Gas Services order backlog of EUR 73bn.

On the Q3 FY2026 earnings call, as reported by Utility Dive: Siemens Energy booked 15 GW of gas turbine orders in the quarter and shipped 6 GW, and its gas turbine backlog stood at 69 GW. CFO Maria Ferraro said 'lead times across the company now run three years or more.' It has about 35 units/yr of large gas turbine capacity, with 15 more planned in 2027. Medium gas turbine capacity is 80 units, rising to about 100 by 2028.

FY2025 results (year to Mar 31, 2026). Large-frame gas turbine orders: 35 units (16 GW), up from 25 units (11 GW) in FY2024. Year-end backlog: 74 units (33 GW), up from 48 units (21 GW). Slide: 'Order intake significantly exceeded last year's record high.' GTCC orders were JPY 2,652.6bn. Briefing Q&A: 'We have a line of sight to increase production capacity by 30% by FY2028' and 'Customers continue to provide us with advanced payments in order to secure production slots.'

Q1 FY2026 (Apr-Jun 2026), as reported by Utility Dive from the Aug 6 briefing. The large-frame gas turbine backlog reached 35 GW, up from 23 GW a year earlier. MHI booked 10 large-frame orders (4 U.S., 6 Japan), scheduled for delivery between 2028 and 2030. CFO Hiroshi Nishio: 'there has been no change in the strong supply-demand environment.' Utility Dive also says MHI 'still plans to double production capacity relative to 2024 levels'; see caveats.
